finding.claim: Broken authorization on project deletion: the handler calls authorized(), which returns a boolean instead of throwing, and discards the result. Any authenticated user can delete any project, including ones they don't own.
finding.source: Any authenticated request user (req.user) sending DELETE /projects/:id with the id of a project owned by someone else.

trace.note: Project is fetched by the attacker-supplied id with no ownership filter.
authorized(req.user, project) returns true or false, and the return value is ignored. Nothing throws.
authorized() only returns a boolean. Unlike authorize() at line 4, it never throws a 403.

finding.guards_checked: The only check on this path is authorized(), and its result is discarded. The PUT route at line 25 correctly uses authorize(), which throws. I saw no router-level or middleware ownership check in api.js. Authentication of req.user is assumed to happen upstream, outside this file. If there is no authentication either, the exposure is wider.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean, and its result is discarded at api.js:18. There is no router-level or middleware check in the directory. The throwing authorize() at api.js:4 is used only on the PUT route (api.js:25).
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls the boolean-returning authorized() (defined at api.js:12) as a bare statement, so the delete at api.js:19 runs for any authenticated user regardless of ownership.
